response.justification: Strong, broad senior engineer with genuine geospatial/GIS domain exposure (GISCollective, Green Map) and proven low-latency, high-throughput backend work at Sociomantic using D with async I/O, fibers, and caching — which maps conceptually onto the performance and distributed-systems demands of a routing pipeline. However, the core hard requirement of modern C++ (or Rust) is barely met: C/C++ appears only in a 7-month role at National Instruments over a decade ago and a university thesis project, with no Rust at all. Recent years have been predominantly TypeScript/Node full-stack and product work, and there is no navigation guidance, map tiling, or routing-data experience. Could be worth a screen if the team values systems fundamentals and fast language ramp-up over immediate C++ productivity, but the language and domain gap is substantial for a mid-senior IC expected to own critical pipeline components.
strengths: Real geospatial/GIS platform experience, including an open-source map data platform he founded
Proven low-latency, high-scale service work (millions of req/sec, async I/O, fibers, caching)
Polyglot systems-minded engineer with strong testing/TDD, CI/CD, Linux, and Kubernetes background
concerns: Modern C++ experience is minimal and over a decade old; no Rust experience listed
No navigation, routing, or map-tiling pipeline experience whatsoever
Recent roles are web/full-stack TypeScript-focused, not systems or data-pipeline engineering
